Q: Excel formula LIKE, AND, IF, WILDCARDS A:

The biggest problem here is the lack of a "Like /Alike" operator or function in excel. Fortunately there is one in VBA.

Public Function LikeText(ByVal ThisText As String, MatchWith As String) As Boolean

     LikeText = IIf(ThisText Like MatchWith, True, False)

End Function

I use it for pattern matching the way I use it for field level data validation in access...

debug.Print LikeText("2026-03-04", "####-##-##")

' confirms that I have a valid date

This doesn't directly solve the questioner's problem. It does however offer alternative approaches

Q: How to cmake, make and compile C++14 on Windows A:

Using Visual Studio compiler

Following Chris Drew comment, here's what I did in order to compile using CMake to generate a Visual Studio 2015 solution and compile this solution in command line.

Note that this is not using the GNU toolchain as we won't be using gcc / make but the Visual C++ Compiler.

Creating and moving to a build subdirectory (it's recommended since it will generate a lot of files, instead of just a standard Makefile) :

mkdir build && cd build

Generating the Visual Studio 2015 solution :

cmake . -G"Visual Studio 14 2015"

This will generate several project files including YourProjectName.sln that we will use to build the project using the following command :

msbuild YourProjectName.sln

Note that msbuild was not in my PATH, so I had to provide the complete path to the executable wich was, in my case, C:\Program Files (x86)\MSBuild\14.0\Bin\MSBuild.exe.

Using an updated MinGW installer

Tive provided a link to a bundled installer that will automatically install GCC 5.1 on your system, this way you can use the normal GNU toolchain by generating an Unix Makefile, and using the make command.

Note that you will need to edit your PATH manually as the installer is not doing it for you.

Q: How to return row where items are grouped by Id and related reference fields? A:

We can consider this task as follows:

  • find the root nodes of the tree that have child nodes
  • and also find the next node in the tree.

Nodes linked by rule Child.Ref1 = left(parent.Ref2, len(Child.Ref1))

Recursive query

WITH r AS(
     SELECT 0 as lvl,t.GroupId,t.ItemId,t.Ref1,t.Ref2
     FROM @test t
     WHERE ref1 is null  -- root node
       AND exists (      -- node have child node
           SELECT 1 from @test t2 
           WHERE t2.GroupId=t.GroupId 
                 AND t2.ref1=left(t.ref2,len(t2.ref1))
            )
     UNION ALL
     SELECT lvl+1 as lvl,r.GroupId,t.ItemId,t.Ref1,t.Ref2
     FROM r INNER JOIN @test t ON r.GroupId=t.GroupId 
       AND t.Ref1 = left(r.Ref2, len(t.Ref1))
       AND lvl<1 -- limit number of childs {0,1}
   )
SELECT * FROM r ORDER BY GroupId,ItemId;

The difference from the query option you provided is an additional check in the anchor part of the recursive query - checking the existence of a child node.
If there is no suitable child node, then the root node is not included in the selection.

Q: Removing duplicates in lists A:

Super late answer:

If you don't care about the list order, you can use *arg expansion with set uniqueness to remove duplicates, i.e. :

l = [*{*l}]
